leak.settled_window: 40-60 s after the peak of the hold
leak.history_comparison: the settled 40-60 s slope (-9.25) is below the 11-18..11-21 plateau (-11.11/-11.36/-11.64/-11.13) for the first time, and the whole-hold slope also fell (-19.14 vs -24.88). The first leak attempt of the day aborted on a single raw=0 sample, see leak_first_attempt.

leak_first_attempt.error: RuntimeError('invalid calibration or extreme raw signal')
leak_first_attempt.detail: one sample carried raw=0 (est 0.0) inside the hold window; both bridge implementations raise "invalid calibration or extreme raw signal" when an active acquisition sees raw < 1000, so the attempt died. A retry under the same conditions completed normally. No other file in the 1180-file corpus contains a raw < 1000 sample.

zero_arc_note: today opened without a latched fault (code=0 NONE, ADSdiag errors=0 recoveries=0), unlike D6 which opened with SENSOR_INIT. The zero came in at +0.78 and the four-state probe settled at -0.29, i.e. within the batch range and comfortably inside the +/-5.0 pre-capture gate.

valve_width_detail.note: the blended flow halved (0.32042 -> 0.17630) and both widths moved the same way: 3 ms 0.30417 -> 0.11042, 4 ms 0.33667 -> 0.24219. This is the largest single-day move of the batch and it is not a single-width outlier.

no_temperature_reason: dropped from the card on 2026-11-18 at the operator request (no thermometer with one-decimal resolution). Kept null rather than back-filled; see crosstday_d03_20261118.md section 1.2.
profile_note: unlike the D6 warning, the profile was found in mode=normal this morning (readback at 12:19: "[Profile] mode=normal ..."), so the round-level "set peak on site" path applies again today. The D6 note that the profile might survive as peak across days therefore did not materialise.
switching_note: the OmniProbe app was not running at first (port 8765 refused), so the open check went over the direct COM6 link. By the profile probe the app had come up and every later command used BRIDGE using OmniProbe 127.0.0.1:8765. No COM12 wake-up was needed.
